body.x: UzBRAINNET (CEO Yoo-seok Won, www.uzbrainnet.co.kr) is set to preview its Rain-Gun, a wireless gaming gun device, and its wearable MotionRing at CES 2015, which runs Jan. 6-9 in Las Vegas.

The Rail-Gun is intended to enhance the experience of FPS (First Person Shooter) gamers and can be used without a keyboard or mouse. The Rail-Gun comes equipped with four units to track the movement of the user. The device is sensitive with high recognition and has the capabilities to detect things such as the unique movements of individual users, when the aim of the user has exited the monitor, any trembling in the user’s hands, and can even automatically rotate the screen.

The wearable MotionRing is equipped with a movement detector to recognize 3D space allowing the user to make a variety of creative contents. It can freely connect, via Bluetooth, to a PC, smartphone, smart TV, and other devices to track the user’s motion.
A spokesperson for UzBRAINNET stated, “We plan to meet with the world’s leading VR and wearable device companies at CES 2015 to find partners to share technology and other avenues of collaboration.”

UzBRAINNET is an IT research and development company not only specializing in applications and software but hardware design technology. It attended last year’s G-STAR where it received prominent attention.

Held annually in January and owned and produced by the Consumer Electronics Association (CEA), CES 2015 is the world's largest IT and consumer electronics exhibition to see the latest global trends in consumer electronics industry in one spot.

Globally recognized for its record in the number of published articles for CES, AVING News has been sending its reporters to CES every year to deliver the fastest and freshest news on the spot. This year, AVING News is using smartphones for news reporting, in line with the trend of one-person media.
